text.p: Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco was banned until 2000 on Monday after testing positive for the anabolic steroid stanozolol at a meeting in the Netherlands last May.
The decision was taken by a three-man International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) arbitration panel.

Capobianco, 26, tested positive at a meeting in Hengelo on May 27 last year for stanozolol, the drug used by Ben Johnson when he tested positive after winning the 1988 Seoul Olympics 100 metres final.
He escaped an automatic four-year ban when the Australian governing body cleared him on the grounds that the testing procedures had been seriously flawed.
The IAAF opposed the Australian decision but allowed Capobianco to compete at last year's Atlanta Olympics after their legal advisors said the federation could be sued successfully in a civil court.
Capobianco was eliminated in the second round of the 200 metres in Atlanta.
In a statement on Monday, the IAAF said Capobianco would be banned until May 27, 2000, four years after the Hengelo meeting and only months before the Sydney Olympics.
"As a consequence of this judgment, all results obtained by Capobianco after May 27, 1996, are declared invalid," the statement said.
